page: Amazon Web Services r9g.medium is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU with 1 thread per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, supporting hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions.

The instance provides 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU ratio typical of memory-optimized profiles. The server does not bundle local disk storage and relies on network-attached options, supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark results reveal top-tier single-threaded capability, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 2294.0 and gzip compression speeds of 36.37 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics and uncached memory throughput place in lower quartiles due to the single-thread execution limit and an uncached large-block write speed of 12.05 GB/sec.

Qualitatively, the r9g.medium delivers an efficient resource footprint for memory-bound tasks that do not justify multi-core overhead. The primary architectural tradeoff lies in raw aggregate throughput, where database operations and static web serving remain bounded by the single-core allocation. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for lightweight Redis caching, single-threaded batch processing, small-scale microservices, and staging environments requiring dedicated CPU consistency paired with elevated memory capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. The instance provides 1 dedicated vCPU operating at 3.3 GHz alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8-to-1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache, with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, reaching top-tier ratings in Geekbench single-core scoring and compression workloads like gzip and bzip3. However, multi-core capacity and uncached memory write throughput remain limited due to the single-core topology. The instance delivers cost-effective resource allocation for workloads requiring dedicated per-core responsiveness and elevated memory allocations without requiring multi-threaded parallelism. Appropriate use cases include lightweight caching tiers, small in-memory databases, microservices, and single-threaded data transformation jobs.
